description: Type Resend's errors per operation. The spec declares no errors, so every failure surfaced as a bare status class or UnknownResendError. Each class matches Resend's machine-readable `name` (core's matcher `code` is numeric, so the name is matched as `body: {"/name": ...}`), with the status and, where one name covers several cases, the message, from Resend's error reference (api-reference/errors) and the live runs of 2026-10-29. Each operation lists the errors it alone can answer: idempotency, the sending quota, sender and recipient refusals, the not-founds of the resources it addresses, and state refusals. State errors match name, status and message, so they win over the generic class with the same name: a broadcast refuses edits, sends, deletes and cancels by status, and a sent broadcast can never be deleted; an email that is no longer scheduled can't be rescheduled or canceled (EmailNotScheduled); a draft sends once (InboxDraftAlreadySent); an inbox address must be on a domain the team has added (DomainNotInTeam); a domain with no claim answers 404 "Domain claim not found" (DomainClaimNotFound). The quota errors carry no httpError, so they get no throttling category and the default retry policy does not wait out a quota that resets at midnight; rate_limit_exceeded stays core's retried TooManyRequests. The errors every operation can answer (auth, validation, resource lock) are declared once, in src/errors.ts.
